name: Metric and Topological Spaces
strandNote: Not needed to be hired. Fixed-point arguments in research papers.
description: Generalise distance to open sets, and prove the contraction mapping theorem.

requires.why: Reuses the metric space axioms, open and closed sets and compactness from real analysis.

lessonObjectives.l1-many-distances: Compare Euclidean, taxicab and maximum metrics, and draw their unit balls.
lessonObjectives.l2-open-balls: Prove that open balls are open and that unions of open sets are open.
lessonObjectives.l3-closure-interior-boundary: Find the closure, interior and boundary of a set.
lessonObjectives.l4-continuity-by-open-sets: Prove that a map is continuous exactly when preimages of open sets are open.
lessonObjectives.l5-topologies: Check the topology axioms, including spaces with no metric.
lessonObjectives.l6-bases-and-subspaces: Build a topology from a basis and give a subset the subspace topology.
lessonObjectives.l7-homeomorphisms: Prove two spaces are homeomorphic, or find a property that tells them apart.
lessonObjectives.l8-connectedness: Prove that intervals are connected, and derive the intermediate value theorem from it.
lessonObjectives.l9-open-covers: Prove a set is compact with open covers, and prove Heine-Borel on the line.
lessonObjectives.l10-compact-images: Prove that a continuous image of a compact set is compact.
lessonObjectives.l11-complete-spaces: Prove a space is complete, or find a Cauchy sequence with no limit in it.
lessonObjectives.l12-contraction-mapping: Prove the contraction mapping theorem without notes.
lessonObjectives.l13-fixed-point-iteration: Use the contraction mapping theorem to show a fixed-point iteration converges, and bound its error.
